THE WOMAN - the headline change. Mark 5:28 records what she said to herself, and
this build had it only as narrator paraphrase ('She did not ask permission. She
did not make a speech.'). It is now w28, PINK, verbatim:
  w28  Mark 5:28  'If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.'
Quoted without Mark's frame 'For she said,' so the caption is her own voice.
This is the only line the woman gets in the whole chapter and the video was
telling her story without ever letting her speak.

exchange instead of a monologue:
  s31  Mark 5:31  'Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou,
                   Who touched me?'  SCRIPTURE (blue - this is the twelve, not Jesus)

gains a one-line retelling of w28 in front of its original sentence. n4c is

WHY-LAW: she reached in secret and he refused to let the healing stay secret -
he stopped a crowd, on his way to a dying child, to give one untouchable woman
a name. Milk framing: he stops for the one, and calls her daughter.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There was a woman who had been suffering for twelve years.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She had spent everything on doctors. Nothing helped. She was exhausted, desperate — and by the rules of her time, considered untouchable.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That day, Jesus was already on his way to save someone else — a ruler's daughter, twelve years old, and dying. The crowd pressed around him on every side. Almost no one would have noticed one more sick woman at its edge.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She heard Jesus was nearby. She did not ask permission. She did not make a speech. She said only one thing, and she said it to herself.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If I can just touch his clothes, she told herself, I will be well. That was the whole of her plan. She pressed through the crowd and reached out to touch the edge of his cloak.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stopped. He had felt it — power had gone out of him. The healing was already hers, given the moment she touched him.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His disciples thought the question made no sense. The whole crowd was pressing against him — who hadn't touched him? He ignored them. He was already needed somewhere else, and he stopped anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He looked for her until he found her.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Be whole of thy plague — be free of what has been hurting you. Twelve years of it. Over, in a sentence. And the first word he chose was daughter.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Whatever you have carried for years — reach for him. He stops for the one. He calls you his own.

stills_wanted.S4: S4 now carries her decision AND her own verbatim words — the moment before she moves, not the moment she hears. Frame her close: a veiled woman at the edge of a moving crowd, head down, lips just parted, one hand already lifting from under her shawl. Everything about her hidden except the intent. Warm dusty light from the street beyond, her face in shadow.
stills_wanted.S8: S8 now carries the disciples' verbatim objection and its retelling. Frame the twelve, not the woman: two or three men close around Jesus, hands open in bafflement, gesturing back at the packed street behind them. Confusion, not anger. The crowd behind them a blur of shoulders — the whole point is that everybody was touching him.
